title: Classic Sashimi and Sushi Platter: Salmon and Tuna Sashimi, Nigiri and Hosomaki
summary: A Japanese-style platter of salmon and tuna sashimi, hand-shaped salmon, tuna and prawn nigiri and a short salmon roll, served with wasabi, pickled ginger and soy sauce.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
large cooked peeled prawns, tails on, butterflied

steps.title: Wash the rice
steps.text: Rinse the rice in a sieve under cold water, swirling it with your fingers, until the water is nearly clear, then leave it to drain for 15 min. Removing loose surface starch stops the grains turning gluey and lets each one stay distinct.

steps.title: Cook and rest
steps.text: Bring the rice and 240 ml water to the boil in the heavy pan, cover tightly and turn the heat right down for 12 min. Take it off the heat and leave the lid on for another 10 min so the steam finishes the centre of each grain.

steps.title: Season the rice
steps.text: Warm the vinegar, sugar and salt in a small pan just until clear. Tip the rice into the wide bowl, pour the seasoning over and cut through it with the paddle while fanning, so the surface turns glossy instead of wet; stop at body temperature and cover with a damp cloth.

steps.title: Slice the fish
steps.text: Using a long, very sharp knife and one smooth pull per cut, take 4 thin 4 mm slices for nigiri from each block, then a 1 cm strip of salmon for the roll. Cut what is left into 1 cm sashimi pieces across the grain and return everything to the fridge, as cold fish cuts and tastes cleanest.

steps.title: Shape the nigiri
steps.text: Wet your hands, gently squeeze about 25 g rice into a small firm oval and smear a little wasabi on one fish slice. Drape the slice over the rice, wasabi side down, and press lightly with two fingers so it hugs the rice without crushing it; repeat with salmon, tuna and prawns.

steps.title: Roll the hosomaki
steps.text: Lay the half nori sheet shiny side down on the mat and spread about 70 g rice thinly over it, leaving a 1 cm strip clear at the far edge. Put the salmon strip along the near edge, roll firmly with the mat and dab the bare edge with water to seal, then cut into 6 with a damp knife.

steps.title: Arrange and serve
steps.text: Fan the sashimi on the platter beside the nigiri and roll pieces, with mounds of wasabi and ginger and small bowls of soy sauce. Serve straight away, while the rice is still slightly warm and the fish cold.

tips: Dip nigiri fish side down into the soy sauce; dipping the rice side makes it soak up too much and fall apart.
Keep a bowl of water with a splash of rice vinegar nearby and wet your hands and knife often, so the rice does not stick.
Ask the fishmonger for neat blocks (saku) cut from the loin, which give the cleanest slices.
safety: RAW NOTE: the fish is eaten raw. Buy sushi- or sashimi-grade fish from a fishmonger you trust that has been frozen first (-20 °C for 7 days or -35 °C for 15 hours), keep it in the fridge until the last minute and eat it the same day. Pregnant people, young children, older adults and anyone with weakened immunity should skip it.
storage: Sashimi and sushi cannot be stored; eat them within an hour of making and discard leftovers. Do not chill the seasoned rice, as it hardens. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
